_comment: Which object in props.glb becomes which prop in the game.
The key is the OBJECT NAME in Blender. Name an object after a prop type -- pine, fir, birch,
rock, boulder, rail, hut, lamp, sign, snowman, fence -- and it is picked up with no entry here
at all; a trailing .001 or _2 is ignored, so pine, pine.001 and pine_2 are three variants of
the same prop and the game will spread them across the forest. This file exists for exports
that still have Blender's default names in them.
SIZE: give ONE of `height`, `length` or `width`, in metres. `height` suits anything defined by
how tall it is; `length` suits anything defined by how long it is -- a rail is a rail because
it is nine metres long, not because of how high off the snow you built it. Either way the
scale stays UNIFORM, so how big you modelled it does not matter, only its proportions do.
`skip` leaves an object out entirely. Run: node tools/asset-check.mjs

Nothing is ever stretched. A prop is scaled UNIFORMLY, and whatever it then measures is what the game uses -- a modelled rail overwrites the rail's width, height and length, so the board rides the rail you built rather than one squashed to fit.
